content: George Brown College (GBC) is a publicly funded and fully accredited institution specializing in applied arts and technology. It operates three main campuses located in downtown Toronto, Ontario. The college was established in 1967 by the government of Ontario, as part of a broader initiative to expand access to post-secondary education in the province. The institution is named after George Brown, a prominent 19th-century politician, newspaper publisher (founder of the Toronto Globe, which later became The Globe and Mail), and one of the Fathers of Confederation. George Brown College offers a diverse range of academic programs across various disciplines, including art and design, business, community services, early childhood education, construction and engineering technologies, health sciences, hospitality and culinary arts, and preparatory studies. Additionally, the college provides specialized programs and services tailored to the needs of recent immigrants and international students. Its academic offerings include 66 diploma programs, five degree programs (one of which is offered in collaboration with Ryerson University), 45 certificate programs, and 33 post-graduate programs. Furthermore, the college provides over 1,000 continuing education courses, catering to a wide range of learners. Currently, George Brown College serves approximately 14,000 full-time students and over 55,000 part-time and continuing education students. It is also recognized as the largest provider of distance education in Canada, with 12,000 students enrolled in programs across more than 30 countries. Among its distance education offerings, the Electronics Technician program is particularly notable, having received multiple awards for its excellence. Casa Loma Campus The Casa Loma campus is the largest of George Brown College's campuses. It is located along Kendal Avenue, between Davenport Road and MacPherson Avenue, in close proximity to landmarks such as Casa Loma and the City of Toronto Archives. The campus is easily accessible, with the Dupont subway station (on the Yonge-University-Spadina line) just a three-minute walk away. The campus consists of five buildings, which include: The Dentistry building. The main campus building, located at 160 Kendal Avenue. The ESL and Building Technologies building. The new Student Centre building, located at 146 Kendal Avenue. The Finance and Student Records building, located at 500 MacPherson Avenue. In 2004, the campus underwent a significant transformation when the old and unused A Building was demolished to create a green space for students and staff. St. James Campus The St. James campus comprises three buildings. The first is a large, uniquely shaped brick building located at 200 King Street East. The second and third buildings are situated at 290 and 300 Adelaide Street East, respectively, and are interconnected. This campus houses programs in Financial Services, Creative Arts Business Administration, and the Faculty of Hospitality and Tourism. It is also home to the college's renowned Chef School. Ryerson University Campus The Ryerson University campus is an affiliated site consisting of offices and classrooms located within Kerr Hall at Ryerson University. The address for this campus is 99 Gerrard Street East. The college's sports teams are known as the Huskies.
